text.p: BIRTHDAYS
English actor EDMUND KEAN, known for his particular interpretations of the roles of "Shylock" and "Richard III", was born in 1787.
Bishop FREDERIC BARKER, who became the Anglican Bishop of Australia and was nicknamed "the high priest" (he was 6-feet 5-inches tall), was born in 1808.
The Catholic Bishop of Queensland JAMES QUINN was born in 1819.
Pioneer German car-maker and engineer GOTTLIEB DAIMLER was born in 1834.
Artist LLOYD REES, known as the "grand old man of Australian art", was born in _ Brisbane in 1895.
American golfer and the first amateur to win the British Open (Lytham St Annes 1926), BOBBY JONES, was born in 1902.

American singer and pianist NAT "KING" COLE, was born in 1917. His first hit was "Straighten Up And Fly Right" (1944). This was followed by "I Love You For Sentimental Reasons" (1946), "The Christmas Song" (1946), "Nature Boy" (1948), "Mona Lisa" (1950), "Too Young" (1951), "Pretend" (1953), "A Blossom Fell" (1955), "When I Fall In Love" (1957) and "Ramblin' Rose" (1962). He died in 1965 from cancer.
Russian ballet dancer RUDOLPH NUREYEV, who literally leapt to international fame when he defected to the West and became the dancing partner of DAME MARGOT FONTEYN, was born in 1938.
The man who had a million seller with the theme song from "Welcome Back, Kotter", JOHN SEBASTIAN was born in 1944.
UK guitarist with 'Thin Lizzy' SCOTT GORHAM was born in 1951.
American actor KURT RUSSELL was born in 1951.
EVENTS

464 - SAINT PATRICK died, urging his gathered friends to have a drink of something to ease their pain. It's claimed that the patron saint of Ireland drove snakes and other venemous beasts from the country by banging a drum, and did so well that any such creature would die if it touched Irish soil.
An Irish businessman is reported to have brought a load of Irish soil to Australia last century to spread around his house and ward-off snakes and the like. (Historic VAUCLUSE HOUSE in Sydney).
1845 - British man STEPHEN PERRY patented the rubber band.
1899 : A merchant ship that ran aground off the English
coast sent the first radio distress call (mayday).
1921 : Britain's first 'Birth Control' centre was opened
in North London, offering advice to women on how to avoid having 1938 : A British committee recommended that flogging
should be abolished.
1943 : In his yearly review General MacARTHUR said
Australia had envisaged the north of the country falling into Japanese hands.
1958 : Australian-born polar explorer SIR GEORGE WILKINS
died.
1959 : The American submarine "SKATE" completed its under-ice voyage to surface at the North Pole.
1968 : Violent demonstrations raged outside the United
States Embassy in London, in opposition to American involvement in the Vietnam War.
1969 : A 70 year-old grandmother, GOLDA MEIR, took Office as Israel's first woman Prime Minister.
1983 : British Prime Minister MARGARET THATCHER was
targetted by the IRA in a letter-bomb campaign.
1991 : Soviet voters went to the polls to decide whether
to 'break-up' into member States or maintain the Soviet "Union".
